message.content:
{
  "frontend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Implement a migration of the UI to submit and display the alias field named "name" instead of using "title". Do not change backend contracts beyond what is specified here; follow these precise rules and tests.

Scope (apply to list, detail, create, update flows):
- Display: always read and display the resource's value from the response field name (response.name). The API will also return response.title, but the UI must use name for all displays.
- Submission for create: the client must send only the JSON property name (omit title entirely). Create requests must include name and must satisfy validation before sending.
- Submission for update: when the user edits the title/name, send only the JSON property name (omit title). If the user does not change the name, do not include name (and do not include title) in the update payload; sending no field means "no change". It is acceptable for update requests to omit both fields per backend rules.
- Never send both name and title in the same request. If both would be present in any client-side object, remove title before sending.

Client-side validation (mirror backend constraints exactly):
- Accepted values: JSON string type only. Null is invalid (reject and do not send).
- Length: minimum 1 character, maximum 255 characters. Do not perform automatic trimming; treat whitespace characters as valid content and count them toward length.
- If validation fails, block the request and surface an inline validation error to the user.

Error handling / expected responses:
- Treat HTTP 422 responses from the server as validation-level failures. Show the server-provided validation message to the user if present.
- Implement UI tests to assert the exact validation behavior described below.

Tests / acceptance cases the frontend must cover (automated unit or integration tests):
1) Create happy path: enter a string length 1..255 (including leading/trailing spaces) -> client validates -> submit { "name": "..." } -> server returns a resource JSON including both title and name and both values are identical -> UI displays response.name.
2) Create failure cases (client-side): empty string or length 0 -> validation blocks submission; null value -> validation blocks submission; length >255 -> blocks submission.
3) Server 422 cases: if server returns 422 (conflict or validation), display server message; ensure UI does not retry automatically.
4) Update happy path: edit name, client validates, send PATCH/PUT payload containing only { "name": "..." } -> server returns resource with both title and name identical -> UI displays updated response.name.
5) Update no-change: do not include name in update payload (user left it unchanged) -> server accepts and leaves DB title untouched -> UI displays the name from the response (which will match DB title).
6) Conflict (should be returned by backend if both fields ever arrive): ensure the client does not generate such a request; add a test that the client never sends both fields.

Payload examples (to be used in tests; do not hardcode endpoint paths in these examples; use the existing create/update endpoints):
- Create request body: { "name": "Example" }
- Create response body (server must return): { "id": <id>, "title": "Example", "name": "Example", ... }
- Update request body: { "name": "Updated" }
- Update response body: { "id": <id>, "title": "Updated", "name": "Updated", ... }

Developer notes:
- Do not send title in any new submissions. Existing code paths that still send title should be updated or removed so that outgoing payloads never include title together with name.
- Keep client-side validation rules identical to backend rules (no trimming, whitespace allowed). This prevents unnecessary 422 responses.
- Add or update automated tests described above in the UI test suite to prevent regressions.

Do not assume any undocumented server behavior. The frontend must rely on the documented contract: responses will include both title and name (identical values) and the server will enforce the validation rules and return 422 for invalid/conflicting payloads."
  },
  "backend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Implement request parsing, validation, persistence-mapping, and response shaping to support a new alias field name for title while keeping the title column in the database unchanged. Follow these precise rules; do not change unspecified contracts.

Request handling (create and update endpoints already existing in the codebase):
- Accepted incoming JSON properties: optional name and optional title.
- Conflict rule: if a request contains both name and title properties (both present in the JSON body), immediately reject with HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity. Do not attempt to reconcile or prefer one over the other.
- Null handling: if either property is present and the JSON value is null, reject with HTTP 422. Explicit null is invalid.
- Presence requirements:
  - Create: request must include at least one of name or title (and not both). If neither name nor title is present, reject with HTTP 422.
  - Update: request may include neither (meaning no change). If it includes one of name or title, apply validation and persist change.
- Validation rules (applied to whichever single field is present):
  - Type must be string. Non-string values -> 422.
  - Length must be between 1 and 255 characters inclusive. Do not trim the value before validation; all characters (including whitespace) count. Empty string length 0 -> 422. >255 -> 422.

Persistence mapping:
- The database schema remains the same; continue to store the canonical value in the existing title column.
- When a request provides name (and not title), write the provided name value into the title column.
- When a request provides title (and not name), write the provided title value into the title column.
- For update requests that omit both fields, do not change the title column.

Response shaping (for list, detail, create, update responses):
- All responses that return resource objects must include both properties title and name.
- Both title and name must contain exactly the same string value, taken from the DB title column for that resource. Do not attempt to mask or canonicalize differently—the two fields must be identical.
- For list endpoints, ensure every resource object in the collection includes both fields identical.

Error handling and status codes:
- For validation or conflict errors described above (both present, explicit null, wrong type, length out of bounds, create missing both), return HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity.
- Response body for 422 should include machine-readable and human-readable error details per existing API error format. If your project has a standard error envelope, use it; otherwise return a JSON object describing the field-level error (which field and why). Do not invent a new status code or different semantic for these errors.

Tests / automated verification (must be added to unit/integration test suites):
1) Create success: POST with { "name": "A" } where length 1..255 -> resource persisted to title column; response includes { "title": "A", "name": "A" }.
2) Create success with title: POST with { "title": "A" } -> persisted to title column; response includes both fields identical.
3) Create failure - both present: POST with { "name": "A", "title": "A" } -> 422.
4) Create failure - missing both: POST with {} -> 422.
5) Create failure - explicit null: POST with { "name": null } (or { "title": null }) -> 422.
6) Create failure - non-string: POST with { "name": 123 } -> 422.
7) Create failure - empty string: POST with { "name": "" } -> 422.
8) Create failure - too long: POST with { "name": "x" * 256 } -> 422.
9) Update success: PATCH/PUT with { "name": "B" } -> title column updated to "B"; response includes both fields identical.
10) Update success - no change: PATCH/PUT with {} -> no change to title column; response includes both fields identical for the resource.
11) Update failure - both present: PATCH/PUT with both fields -> 422.
12) List/detail responses: ensure each returned resource object contains title and name identical (unit/integration tests assert equality).

Examples to include in tests and docs (use your existing endpoint paths):
- Valid create request body: { "name": "Example" }
- Valid create response body: { "id": 123, "title": "Example", "name": "Example", ... }
- Valid update request body: { "name": "Updated" }
- Valid update response body: { "id": 123, "title": "Updated", "name": "Updated", ... }
- Invalid request (both): { "name": "A", "title": "A" } -> 422
- Invalid request (null): { "name": null } -> 422

Developer notes and constraints:
- Do not add automatic trimming of input anywhere. Validation uses raw submitted string length.
- Do not add a new database column; continue to write to title.
- Do not change any other fields in the resource representation besides adding (or ensuring presence of) name in responses.
- Keep response content for other fields unchanged.
- Ensure backward compatibility: clients that still submit title-only continue to work; newly migrated clients submit name-only.
- Add comprehensive tests to prevent regressions and to assert that response.title === response.name in all endpoints listed (list, detail, create, update).

Do not invent behaviors not specified above. If any aspect of request/response envelope (error format, authenticated behavior, endpoint paths, HTTP method specifics) is not already defined in your project, integrate these rules into the existing routes and error conventions rather than creating new conventions."
  }
}
